`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The strongest clue in this batch is textual: the Container and Deployment views reuse component-edge labels verbatim ("Appends ordered bounded events and cleanup state"). Structurizr's default implied-relationship strategy creates a container-level edge from the first component edge it sees and then suppresses later ones, so whichever component relationship was written first in the DSL silently becomes the container's public description. Explicit container edges fix this.
- Dynamic views in Structurizr can only traverse relationships that exist in the static model. That is why P3-F04 and P3-F06 matter beyond labeling: if McpServer has no static read edge, a callback-read step cannot be drawn later without changing the model.
- The SVGs are PlantUML exports of the Structurizr model (per-word `<text>` elements with ` ` spacers). That satisfies "editable vector text" literally, but edits are clumsy and the creole `<size:24>` tags leak into `<title>`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The strongest clue in this batch is textual: the Container and Deployment views reuse component-edge labels verbatim ("Appends ordered bounded events and cleanup state"). Structurizr's default implied-relationship strategy creates a container-level edge from the first component edge it sees and then suppresses later ones, so whichever component relationship was written first in the DSL silently becomes the container's public description. Explicit container edges fix this.
- Dynamic views in Structurizr can only traverse relationships that exist in the static model. That is why P3-F04 and P3-F06 matter beyond labeling: if McpServer has no static read edge, a callback-read step cannot be drawn later without changing the model.
- The SVGs are PlantUML exports of the Structurizr model (per-word `<text>` elements with ` ` spacers). That satisfies "editable vector text" literally, but edits are clumsy and the creole `<size:24>` tags leak into `<title>`.
